exposure: Percutaneous balloon mitral valvuloplasty (PBMV) during antenatal care
outcome: Maternal outcomes (pulmonary edema, medical termination of pregnancy, hypothyroidism, hepatitis B infection, pneumonia, postprocedural delivery, postprocedure severe mitral regurgitation)
Fetal/Neonatal outcomes (Term birth, mode of delivery, birth weight, Apgar scores at 1, 5, and 10 minutes)
Hemodynamic improvements (Mitral valve area, mitral valve gradient, pulmonary artery systolic pressure)
cohort: The study included 117 pregnant women who underwent percutaneous balloon mitral valvuloplasty (PBMV) for rheumatic mitral stenosis.
finding: PBMV is a safe and effective intervention for mitral stenosis in pregnant women, leading to favorable maternal and short-term neonatal outcomes, with significant hemodynamic improvement and a 100% success rate.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was significantly associated with pregnancy and neonatal outcomes.
followup_time: Short-term neonatal outcomes (Apgar scores at 1, 5, and 10 minutes post-birth); maternal follow-up time not specified.
birth_weight: N/A (birth weight was an outcome measured, not an inclusion criterion for the cohort)
gest_age: The PBMV procedure was performed at a mean gestational age of 22.49 +/- 5.82 weeks (74.36% in the second trimester).
